questions.q: If $0 < x < \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}x}{\alpha} = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}x}{\beta}$, then a value of $sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi\alpha}{\alpha + \beta}\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}x}{\alpha} = \dfrac{\cos^{- 1}x}{\beta} = k$

i.e. $\sin^{- 1}x = k\alpha$ and $\cos^{- 1}x = k\beta$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}x + \cos^{- 1}x = k\left(\alpha + \beta\right)$

i.e. $k\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{\pi}{2\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}$

Now $\dfrac{2\pi\alpha}{\alpha + \beta} = 4k\alpha = 4\sin^{- 1}x$

So $sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi\alpha}{\alpha + \beta}\right) = sin\left(4\sin^{- 1}x\right)$

$= 2sin\left(2\sin^{- 1}x\right)cos\left(2\sin^{- 1}x\right)$

$= 2sin\left(\sin^{- 1}2x\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)cos\left(\sin^{- 1}2x\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)$

$= 2sin\left(\sin^{- 1}2x\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)cos\left(\cos^{- 1}\left(1 - 2{x}^{2}\right)\right)$

$= 4x\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\left(1 - 2{x}^{2}\right)$

questions.q: Let $\left(a, b\right) ⊂ \left(0, 2\pi\right)$ be the largest interval for which $\sin^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right) - \cos^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right) > 0, \theta \in \left(0, 2\pi\right)$, holds . If $\alpha{x}^{2} + \betax + \sin^{- 1}\left({x}^{2} - 6x + 10\right) + \cos^{- 1}\left({x}^{2} - 6x + 10\right) = 0$ and $\alpha - \beta = b - a$, then $\alpha$ is equal to;
questions.solution:
Given, $\sin^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right) - \cos^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right) > 0, \theta \in \left(0, 2\pi\right)$

$∵ \sin^{- 1}\left(\theta\right) + \cos^{- 1}\left(\theta\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$∴ \sin^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right) - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right)\right) > 0$

$\sin^{- 1}\left(sin\theta\right) > \dfrac{\pi}{4} ⇒ \theta \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$

$\left(a, b\right) = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) ⇒ b - a = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Given $b - a = \alpha - \beta$

$∴ \alpha - \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} . . . . . ( 1 )$

Now $\alpha{x}^{2} + \betax + \sin^{- 1}\left({x}^{2} - 6x + 10\right) + \cos^{- 1}\left({x}^{2} - 6x + 10\right) = 0$

Now defining ${x}^{2} - 6x + 10 = 1 + {\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} \ge 1$

Hence $x = 3$ is the only possible solution

$9\alpha + 3\beta + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

On solving equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$ we get,

$\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation $\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 1} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is:
questions.solution:
We have,

$\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 1} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

For equation to be defined,

for $\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)}$,

${x}^{2} + x \ge 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + x + 1 \ge 1 . . . . \left(1\right)$

And, from domain of $\sin^{- 1}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 1}$, ${x}^{2} + x + 1 \le 1 . . . . \left(2\right)$

$∴$ from $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ only possibility that the equation is defined is

${x}^{2} + x = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, - 1$

at $x = 0$, $\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 1} = 0 + \dfrac{\pi}{2} \ne \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

and at $x = - 1$, $\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x\left(x + 1\right)} + \sin^{- 1}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 1} = 0 + \dfrac{\pi}{2} \ne \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

None of these values satisfy

$∴$ Number of roots$= 0$

questions.q: The value of $2sin\dfrac{\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, $2sin\dfrac{\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$

Now by we know that $sin\left(\theta\right) = cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)$, so by using this we get $sin\dfrac{\pi}{22} = cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{22}\right) = cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11}$ and similarly $sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22} = cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}, sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22} = cos\dfrac{3\pi}{11}, sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22} = \dfrac{2\pi}{11}, sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22} = cos\dfrac{\pi}{11}$

So, $2sin\dfrac{\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$

$= 2cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{3\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{1\pi}{11}$

$= 2cos\dfrac{1\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$

{As $cos\dfrac{3\pi}{22} = - cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{11}\right) = - cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}$ and $cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11} = - cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$}

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}{2sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}cos\dfrac{\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}{{2}^{2}sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}{{2}^{3}sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{16\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}{{2}^{4}sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{sin\dfrac{32\pi}{11}}{{2}^{4}sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{16}\dfrac{sin\left(3\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{11}\right)}{sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}} = \dfrac{1}{16}$
